# Oxpull

> Oxpull publishes django-ox, a free, open-source (BSD 3-Clause) worker for Django's Tasks framework. The task queue lives in your existing PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQLite database, so there is no broker to run. Current release: django-ox 1.9.1 (2026-10-17).

Execution is at-least-once. A worker holds a lease on each task it runs; if the worker dies, the lease expires and another worker finishes the task. Enqueue inside `transaction.atomic()` and the task commits or rolls back with your data.

With pooled or persistent connections, django-ox ran 1.4 to 1.7 times the throughput of django-tasks-db 0.13.0 in our benchmark (PostgreSQL 16, no-op tasks, medians of five runs).

## Start here

- [Documentation for AI assistants](https://oxpull.com/django-ox/llms.txt): facts and links, kept current with each release.
- [Full documentation in one file](https://oxpull.com/django-ox/llms-full.txt)
- [Benchmarks](https://oxpull.com/django-ox/benchmarks/): methods, settings and every measured cell.
- [Background tasks, step by step](https://oxpull.com/django-ox/background-tasks/): install, enqueue, run a worker.

## Blog

- [Your customer paid. Then the worker died.](https://oxpull.com/blog/your-customer-paid-then-the-worker-died/): what a dead background worker costs a Django business, and how leases recover the task.
- [Your workers open a new Postgres connection for every task](https://oxpull.com/blog/your-workers-open-a-new-postgres-connection-for-every-task/): connection settings and the matched django-ox and django-tasks-db results.
